note: One position, four jobs, each the same shape turned a new way: over a slow metronome, its roots alone on the whole neck, over a band, then free phrases that end on a root. It states its moves (any key, tempo 60 to 90), so the title and the first step name the key and the tempo as params and no step mentions a selector: the app brings the next key or a faster tempo. The why says what the roots are for, so the learner knows where to end a phrase in any scale.

exercise.title: {{=key}} minor pentatonic, position 1
exercise.why: A phrase sounds finished when it ends on the root, so learn the shape and where its roots sit together: then anything you make up has somewhere to land.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Play position 1 from the lowest {{1}} up to the high E string and back down, one note per beat.
Stay with it until your fingers find the next note without you looking.

Now only the {{1}} notes are in play. Hop between them in any order, until you can go to each one without hunting for it.
In another key the position sits on other frets, and the roots keep their places inside it.
Press Play below to start the band: drums and bass, faster than the metronome was. Play the whole position again, starting from a different {{1}} each time.

Keep the band going and make up short phrases from the position, with a gap after each. End each phrase on {{1}} and hear how it sounds finished. Every note in the position fits this backing, so try anything.
